title: Message from the CEO to Enphase employees
summary: An update on the recent restructuring efforts from Badri Kothandaraman, President and CEO of Enphase Energy.
body_markdown:
#### Introduction


I’m writing to share the restructuring actions we are taking to strengthen Enphase. Market conditions have been more challenging than we anticipated at the beginning of the year, and these actions are necessary to adapt to the current environment while positioning Enphase for long-term success.


The federal 30% Residential Clean Energy Tax Credit (25D) expired on December 31, 2025, eliminating the incentive for homeowners purchasing solar systems with cash or loans beginning in 2026. The impact on the U.S. residential solar industry has been substantial. Our U.S. sell-through declined 35% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, consistent with broader industry trends reported by third-party market research firms. Elevated interest rates have further pressured demand for loan-financed systems, making affordable financing and a compelling customer value proposition more important than ever.


In Europe, policy changes in some of our core markets have created near-term uncertainty, even as they support the industry's long-term development. Competition remains intense, and easing energy security concerns have also weighed on demand.


In response to these challenges, we are taking decisive steps to align our operations and investments with current market realities. This includes reducing our global workforce, concentrating resources on our most important markets, streamlining manufacturing and facilities, and focusing our investments on the five growth drivers outlined in our most recent earnings call.


These are difficult decisions, particularly because they affect talented colleagues who have contributed so much to Enphase. I am deeply grateful for their dedication and the role they have played in building the company we are today. We are committed to treating our departing colleagues with respect and supporting them through this transition, as outlined below.


#### Why we are making these changes


These actions are designed to bring our operating costs in line with current market realities while preserving our ability to invest in the growth opportunities ahead. We remain focused on maintaining a disciplined financial operating model, balancing revenue, gross margin, and operating expenses to achieve sustainable profitability. Today, our non-GAAP operating expenses are approximately $80 million per quarter. Through these restructuring actions and continued cost discipline, we are targeting a reduction to approximately $60–65 million per quarter beginning in the first quarter of 2027. This will establish a leaner cost structure, improve our operating leverage, and position us to return to profitable growth as market conditions recover.


#### Strategic actions


Our actions focus on the areas below:


**Prioritizing innovation for 2027 and beyond:** We are concentrating our investments on five key growth drivers and minimizing distractions: next-generation residential batteries, the recovery of the U.S. residential solar market through innovative financing solutions, expansion into U.S. commercial solar and storage, unidirectional and bidirectional (Bi-Di) EV chargers, and solid-state transformer (SST) technology for data centers.


**Scaling productivity through AI and automation:** We are accelerating the adoption of AI across our core engineering and customer service functions to drive innovation, improve quality, enhance the customer experience, and increase productivity. In engineering, we are leveraging AI to accelerate product development, improve design and testing, detect defects earlier, and reduce rework. In customer service, we are deploying AI-powered virtual assistance, predictive diagnostics, intelligent case routing, and automation to resolve issues faster.


**Concentrating on our core markets:** Earlier this year, we moved several smaller markets to a distribution-led coverage model, supported by adjacent regional teams to maintain strong customer engagement and service. We are taking the same approach in a few additional markets so we can focus our resources where we see the greatest opportunities.


**Consolidating footprint:** We are streamlining our manufacturing operations and consolidating our facilities footprint to reduce fixed costs and improve efficiency. We will optimize capacity utilization, eliminate redundancies, and align our infrastructure with current demand while preserving the flexibility to scale as the business grows.


We expect these actions to result in one-time restructuring and asset impairment charges of approximately $25–28 million.


#### What is not changing


Our commitment to product quality, customer experience, and the success of our installers and channel partners remains unwavering. As we navigate the current environment, we must stay focused on driving revenue, executing with discipline, and delivering value to our customers, while continuing to invest in the strategic priorities that will fuel our long-term growth.


#### Commitment to our people


We have informed approximately 320 impacted employees, with a small number of individual cases remaining. We will treat each person with respect and care, and we are committed to providing transition assistance, severance, and benefits in line with local practices.


#### United States


- Pay will continue through the separation date, generally December 11, 2026 (with exceptions as needed).
- Severance includes a minimum of 13 weeks of pay and accelerated vesting of certain RSUs, subject to applicable approvals.
- Healthcare benefits will remain available through the end of the month of the separation date; employees may elect COBRA continuation coverage at their expense thereafter.
- Employees may coordinate with their managers to use reasonable company time before separation to pursue their next opportunity.


#### Outside the United States


- We will follow local processes and employment laws.
- Where applicable, we intend to maintain a consistent baseline of support across regions, including severance and treatment of equity, aligned with local requirements.


#### Our way forward


**Our priorities are clear:** execute with discipline, leverage AI to drive innovation and efficiency, deliver customer value, and advance our five growth drivers.


I am confident that we will emerge stronger together. Thank you for your resilience, dedication, and commitment to Enphase.


Badri Kothandaraman
President and CEO
Enphase Energy, Inc.


This letter contains forward-looking statements, including, but not limited to, statements related to the restructuring actions and their expected costs; the targeted reduction in non-GAAP operating expenses and its timing; expectations regarding improvements to our cost structure; our ability to align our operations and investments with current market realities; expectations regarding the areas of strategic focus; the use of AI and automation to drive innovation, improve quality, enhance the customer experience, and increase productivity; ability to advance our five growth drivers; and expectations for new products.
